financial_valuation_funding_model.ordinary_returns_status: Suppressed: current price, reliability and material current acquired obligations unresolved. Every projection is an explicit hypothetical, not assurance of current financeability.
design: Parent cash plus a terminal subsidiary EQUITY residual: subsidiary debt, cash and goodwill are not separately added or deducted. Residual subsidiary values of ₹12/35/55 crore are analyst assumptions after modeled dividends, support and tax settlement, not verified fair values.

Opening parent cash is ₹0.9672 crore on 31 March 2026, including ₹0.9311 crore fixed deposits excluded by default because restrictions are unverified. Deposit availability and the reserve are sensitized.

Actual rights receipt is ₹45.30 crore on 7 April: ₹23.30 crore working-capital earmark and ₹10.50 crore acquisition earmark remain restricted. Only the remainder, net of ₹0.1722 crore incremental fees, is unrestricted. The previously prepaid ₹0.5057 crore is not paid again.

Arrowin seller payment of ₹12.04 crore on 13 April uses ₹10.50 crore acquisition earmark and ₹1.54 crore other cash. The March HA & DL payment is already in opening debt/cash. ESOP cash of ₹0.06 crore and 60,000 shares enter only on 26 June.

Opening trade working capital is ₹14.4438 crore. Advances ₹3.1706 crore plus other current assets ₹3.5964 crore, less rights prepayment ₹0.5057 crore and migration prepayment ₹0.0704 crore, leave ₹6.1909 crore conservatively treated as other operating assets. No opening recovery is assumed; growth requires incremental funding.

Old other current liabilities ₹1.2709 crore plus provisions ₹0.4468 crore run off once over the exact 365 days to 31 March 2027. They are not also netted against trade working capital. Subsequent recurring costs remain in EBITDA rather than being charged a second time.

Monthly interval uses are prefunded before EBITDA receipts. Rights and ESOP event rows additionally test the pre-receipt trough; required rescue is dated before the interval. The ₹0.25 crore reserve is an analyst stress, not an observed default. Counterfactual rescue at ₹20 uses whole shares and 3% fees.

Initial parent debt is ₹26.5282 crore; principal repayments are capped at outstanding debt. Short-term facilities roll unless a specified stress calls them. Foreign acquisition tax is tested at ₹0/3/8 crore because the disclosed amount is missing, not because any of these amounts is verified.

No parent dividends are assumed. Subsidiary dividends are included in parent taxable income at a normalized 25% rate. Operating cash, maintenance and growth capex, other assets and support continue through the terminal date.

Terminal operating reserve and reinvestment are preserved. Unused restricted rights and fixed deposits are excluded, not treated as free surplus. No separate property/book-value or goodwill premium is added to operating enterprise value.

The projection starts with hypothetical FY2027 core revenue run-rates of ₹43/48/55 crore. Growth, margins, capital needs and exit multiples are scenario assumptions, not company forecasts or authenticated current financeability.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Maruti Interior Products is Hold — unresolved. The legacy kitchen-hardware franchise is genuine, but the current investment case is not a verified compounder. Headline FY2026 group profit overstates recurring progress: ₹6.6703 crore is a noncash trade-payable write-off, while legacy PAT fell to ₹3.5940 crore and the June quarter weakened sharply.

The actual ₹45.30 crore rights raise is a meaningful recapitalisation, not a hypothetical promise. It also financed a materially different group. Overseas recycling and Arrowin bring additional capital, tax, integration and accounting questions that cannot be resolved by applying a historical hardware P/E.

G2 and G4 are Hold. G1 and G3 are Conditional, not integrity or insolvency failures. BQS, GQS and IAS are incomplete, so no numerical ranking, ordinary IRR, buy price or compounder designation is supported.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
paragraphs: Issuer: Maruti Interior Products Limited, BSE 543464/SPITZE, ISIN INE0JSJ01014, CIN L36998GJ1997PLC031719. SME classification is retained because the 19 October 2026 security master shows the SM row and a 1,000-share lot. A main-board migration application does not establish completed migration.

Information cutoff is 20 October 2026. Annual statements end 31 March 2026; the latest retrieved interim results end 30 June 2026 and were published 8 September. Original financial sources are issuer filings, with some exchange PDFs obtained through a verbatim public mirror. Price is not authenticated: ₹35 is an analyst scenario assumption, never described as the 19 October close.

The intended horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, 1,826 days, using ACT/365.25. The nominal pretax equity hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. The ₹500,000 reference position is illustrative, not a personal suitability conclusion. Historical arithmetic has high traceability; current organic economics, acquisition balances and investability have low confidence.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
paragraphs: GOV 4, MOAT 4, DUR 5, CASH 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 3 are the scoreable factors. REV, CAP, BAL, R, D, P and L remain NS. The same factor appears once in each applicable formula; there is no extra size, order-book or catalyst bonus.

BQS known contribution is 2.82 with 68% original-weight coverage, giving a mathematical missing-data bound of 3.14–6.02. GQS known contribution is 1.85 at 45% coverage, giving 2.40–7.35. These display as 3.1–6.0 and 2.4–7.4 with half-up rounding. IAS has no supported complete input and its mathematical 1–10 bound is not informative.

Incomplete bounds are not midpoints, confidence intervals or rankable quality scores. GOV and CASH one-point judgment changes move BQS by 0.20 and 0.10 respectively; even the favorable joint shift does not resolve evidence gates. Detailed factor facts, contrary evidence, weights and contributions follow in the appendices.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: The company sells functional household hardware rather than interior construction contracts: kitchen storage baskets, drawers, organizers, fittings and related products. Everyday targets economical products and Spitze a higher-priced range. Manufacturing at Shapar, Rajkot, is complemented by OEM supply, dealers/distributors and resale of traded goods.

The economic mix matters. FY2026 raw-material consumption fell while purchased traded stock rose almost 79%; an apparent sales-growth story can therefore be distribution turnover rather than expanded manufacturing volume. Purchases are not sales and cannot be used to infer an exact trading share. No reliable issuer product-level sales/margin or capacity-utilisation bridge was found.

The perimeter changed in March and April 2026. HA & DL Singapore and its Vietnamese Vina Metal business add stainless/recycled-metal production and export exposure. Arrowin moved from an associate to a wholly owned subsidiary. These activities have different input, inventory, foreign-exchange and compliance risks from household hardware.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
paragraphs: Brands, a functioning factory, a broad product range and historical OEM access create useful capability, but not a demonstrated durable moat. The customer base is concentrated: ten customers accounted for 71.95% of FY2025 sales. Supplier concentration at 83.40% further limits independent bargaining power.

Exact repeat retention, qualified long-term contracts, price realisation per unit, competitive win/loss data and sustainably superior product gross margins were not verified. The material trading component makes supplier availability and credit terms important. Dealer relationships can create friction, but substitutable hardware and many competitors constrain pricing.

Management says Vina has a unique BIS permission for relevant exports to India. That claim is not independently authenticated here and is not scored as a legal monopoly or durable cost advantage. The slight reduction in customer concentration is favorable counterevidence.

A limited historical benchmark is Carysil, a much larger sink/appliance manufacturing group. Its FY2025 core EBITDA excluding other income was 16.84% of revenue, CFO/PAT 93.55%, and closing receivable days 65.3. Maruti FY2025 margin was higher at 18.95%, but collection days 99.5 and weaker cash conversion caution against equating accounting margin with moat. Its FY2026 core margin fell to 12.76%. Product, export, scale and Ind AS differences make this an operating comparison, not a market-multiple transfer. [Carysil annual report](https://bsmedia.business-standard.com/_media/bs/data/announcements/bse/16092025/94fcfb43-c9be-4d9a-8d43-2fa983be69fa.pdf)

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
paragraphs: Five-year reported consolidated revenue CAGR is calculated from ₹15.1937 crore in FY2021 to ₹52.6775 crore in FY2026; the three-year cross-check starts from ₹37.9010 crore in FY2023. Both are shown in the derived metrics. The measurement window is chosen before scoring and is not selected for the highest result.

Underlying organic expansion is not reliably established. FY2026 legacy sales rose to ₹52.1411 crore, but raw-material use fell and trading purchases increased. Price, quantity, mix and gross pass-through effects are not separated; the new foreign business and changed Arrowin ownership further disrupt comparability. Consequently REV is NS rather than mechanically assigning the reported-CAGR band.

The June 2026 standalone quarter fell 27.47% in revenue and 68.52% in PAT year on year. Group sales also fell despite consolidation additions. This is a material warning, not enough by itself for a sustained-trajectory score adjustment. No unsupported order-book conversion or rapid-capacity-ramp claim is incorporated.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: Legacy expansion absorbed substantial capital. FY2022–FY2025 capex totaled ₹20.4537 crore against cumulative CFO of ₹8.0815 crore. Plant assets and working capital increased; external equity and debt, rather than retained free cash alone, funded expansion.

The audited legacy incremental-capital proxy is approximately 10.01% for FY2022–FY2025 and 7.56% for FY2023–FY2025, using core EBIT after a 25% normalized tax and invested capital equal to equity plus debt less cash and noncurrent investments. Those figures sit below an analyst 12–16% operating-capital hurdle. They are not project IRRs: cash restrictions, ramp timing and asset classifications limit precision.

Current CAP stays NS because the acquisitions and goodwill cannot be mapped coherently to recurring incremental returns. This is a real perimeter problem, not a blanket demand for private project cohorts. Housing/storage demand provides some runway, but the rights forecast of ₹59.3174 crore net working capital is a management plan and must not be booked as accomplished revenue or committed finance.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
paragraphs: Family management provides continuity but also concentrates decision-making. FY2025 directors’ remuneration was ₹0.96 crore, about one-fifth of owner PAT. ESOP vesting includes market-capitalisation targets, which should be assessed alongside cash and operating performance rather than price alone.

The company completed the disclosed acquisitions and rights issue, and the deal announcements state they are not related-party transactions. Those are favorable facts. However, the AOC-1 ownership label conflicts with dated acquisition timing, investment cash is not fully bridged to consideration, and foreign account preparation delayed successive reporting periods.

Secretarial findings include small filing fines: ₹2,360 for an annual report one day late and ₹22,420 for a complaint statement 19 days late. Management says these were filed and systems strengthened. The issue is recurring execution and disclosure discipline, not the rupee magnitude of the fines. No fraud, tunneling or intentional misstatement is alleged.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: The full FY2025 statutory report is marked by specific adverse findings despite its unmodified main opinion. Auditors did not independently verify inventory and debtor, creditor or advance balances. The audit trail was not maintained. CARO bank-return differences recur, including a ₹0.8909 crore March 2025 creditor discrepancy. Clean IFC and no-default conclusions are retained as contrary evidence; they do not erase those specific findings.

Current assurance is incomplete. The retrieved FY2026 annual-report version contains 97 pages of notice, board material and annexures but no full statutory financial statements. The separate audited results provide main opinions and financial tables, not full CARO/IFC/audit-trail reports. June subsidiary information for all three subsidiaries was management certified and unreviewed by the group auditor. This is a coverage limitation, not proof that full reports were never filed.

FY2026 group cash reconciles to ₹1.3767 crore. Nevertheless, the cashflow’s ₹20.8563 crore investing line is labeled fixed deposits despite matching standalone investment cash; stated acquisition cash considerations differ by ₹1.9043 crore; and associate profit is added to pre-associate PBT in CFO. Acquired working-capital and goodwill movements need a complete reconciliation before cash is treated as organic.

Headline owner PAT ₹10.4425 crore includes ₹6.6703 crore of noncash payable write-off. The cashflow removes that gain, which is appropriate, but details of creditor settlement and tax finality are absent. The small domestic TDS dispute declined from ₹0.97 lakh to ₹0.22 lakh, favorable evidence unrelated to the unquantified foreign pre-acquisition tax liability.

Primary historical CFO/PAT uses PAT before associate earnings to match the operating cashflow perimeter. FY2022–FY2025 conversion is about 53.13%; the owner-PAT ratio is separately labeled about 52.94%. Closing receivable days rose from roughly 63 in FY2024 to 99.5 in FY2025. June group EBIT/interest is about 1.30 times, while annual FY2026 coverage is stronger. No current default is inferred from these warnings.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
paragraphs: No ordinary valuation recommendation is issued. At the explicit ₹35 assumption and 60.46 million actual issued shares, reference market capitalisation is ₹211.61 crore. This is scenario arithmetic, not an observed market quote. FY2026 EPS based on 15.1 million pre-rights shares cannot be multiplied by current shares or treated as current earnings power.

The model uses parent operating cash plus a terminal acquired-subsidiary equity value. That avoids applying core-hardware multiples to one-off creditor income or adding subsidiary cash, debt and acquisition goodwill twice. Terminal subsidiary equity is a scenario residual after modeled dividends, support and tax settlement, not an asserted fair value or an unchanged cost plus distributions.

Opening parent cash ₹0.9672 crore includes ₹0.9311 crore fixed deposits whose restriction status is unverified; the default excludes them and explicitly tests availability. Actual rights cash arrives on 7 April, acquisition seller payment on 13 April and ESOP cash on 26 June. Working-capital and acquisition earmarks cannot fund unrelated debt, capex or tax. Previously prepaid rights costs are not paid again.

Cash is modeled monthly with explicit pre-receipt troughs, incremental trade working capital, recurring advances, interest, taxes, debt amortisation, legacy liabilities, capex and acquired-business support. Terminal reserve remains in the business. Any reserve breach, including before entry, suppresses nonrescue conditional returns. Rescue variants explicitly issue whole shares at an assumed ₹20 with 3% fees before spending; these are counterfactual transactions, not actual or promised funding.

The bear/base/bull assumptions and complete monthly/annual/sensitivity rows are embedded in the canonical dossier. They test mechanisms rather than establish fair value. Reverse expectations are accepted only with finite funded bracket crossings; a failed crossing within the tested growth range is reported as unsolved, never as a required endpoint CAGR.

A second, deliberately conservative earnings cross-check removes all other income and exceptional gains, applies 25% normalized tax and adds the rounded associate earnings contribution. FY2026 owner PAT is then about ₹3.4935 crore, or ₹0.5778 per current share. The assumed ₹35 implies about 60.57 times that proxy. This is not a forward P/E or a target: the year has a partial acquired perimeter and does not include earnings from all later rights cash. Historical reported diluted EPS and its bonus/rights bases are disclosed separately, rather than treating ₹6.92 pre-rights EPS as current earnings power.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
paragraphs: The linked downside is weaker legacy sales plus lower resale/manufacturing margin, slow inventory and receivable conversion, higher interest, a partial credit-line call and foreign pre-acquisition tax. Reserves and rights earmarks can coexist with scarce unrestricted cash. Raising cheap equity can preserve operations while damaging per-share recovery.

The model does not pretend that an analyst reserve breach was an observed default. Actual rights capital is strong positive evidence. The bear path instead shows how a material tax or refinancing call and continuing capital requirements could absorb it. Small disputed domestic TDS and immaterial filing fines are not the reason for the funding concern.

Balance-sheet asset values are not a guaranteed liquidation floor. Inventory and balance verification have explicit audit limitations, recycling assets face different realisation risks, and no separate value is added for property already required by operating earnings. Permanent loss is possible through bad acquired returns, nonrecoverable balances or dilutive funding, even without fraud.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
paragraphs: Over the exact horizon, a 5× price outcome requires approximately 37.98% annual price growth and 10× approximately 58.50%, before personal taxes and execution friction. They are outcome tests, not probability forecasts.

At the ₹35 assumption, 5× and 10× terminal prices are ₹175 and ₹350. Reverse tests vary core growth while retaining capital needs, restricted cash, parent debt, acquired equity residual, issuance fees and dilution. The tested growth bracket runs from negative 5% to positive 80% a year; if no funded crossing exists, no required CAGR is printed.

It is not enough to multiply a small starting PAT by an optimistic multiple. A durable multi-bagger would require independently verified recurring earnings, scalable unit economics, sensible acquired returns and funded growth without disproportionate share issuance. Current evidence does not demonstrate that combination.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
paragraphs: Before reconsideration, obtain the full FY2026 statutory audit report and annexures; inventory and debtor/creditor/advance reconciliation; documented bank-return adjustments and evidence that audit-trail preservation now operates. An unmodified headline audit alone is not the clearance test.

Reconcile the March and April acquisition purchase-price allocations, cash paid versus consideration, Arrowin share counts/ownership dates, foreign goodwill and pre-acquisition tax amounts, due dates and recourse. Obtain rights utilisation and release terms, current facilities, debt maturities and subsidiary cash/obligation bridges.

For business progress, track manufactured volumes versus trading turnover, realized price/mix, concentration and receivable ageing, inventory ageing, core margins, recurring diluted EPS and CFO before exceptional gains. For market access, retrieve dated BSE price/trade history, lot, surveillance status and bid-ask depth. Review the next published results when available, without assuming unreported improvement.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
paragraphs: Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Not ranking eligible and not a compounder candidate. The conclusion is primarily an evidence and investability hold, not a categorical rejection of the products or an allegation of wrongdoing.

No ordinary buy range or expected return is stated. The scenario tables are not alternative actionable targets. Reopen valuation only after the material reliability and funding-perimeter questions are resolved and a current executable price/liquidity basis is authenticated. If subsequent evidence reconciles the accounts, the business can be rescored without carrying forward an unsupported penalty.

Keep the company in the separate SME research universe. No inference is made that a ₹5 lakh position is appropriate for a particular investor, and no trade or public recommendation is authorized by this research.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
paragraphs: Primary source priority is audited issuer statements and dated corporate-action filings, followed by current limited-review information, the rights prospectus and the dated exchange master. CRISIL is useful independent context but its current information gap and stale acquisition/revenue perimeter are explicitly flagged.

Critical open questions are the current full statutory audit annexures; independent inventory and receivable assurance; bank-return reconciliation; acquisition cash, ownership and goodwill mapping; foreign tax quantum; actual usable rights/bank liquidity; organic volume/price demand; and authenticated BSE price/liquidity. Missing values are null/NS, not zero.

All monetary financial facts are in crore unless labeled lakh, rupees per share or share count. Raw financial statements are retained separately from the authored research package. The source-safe package preserves issuer URLs, retrieved document hashes, financial extracts and reproducible calculations, not original PDFs, OCR, personal identifiers or shareholder lists. Reproducing the model validates arithmetic, not authenticity of unavailable original evidence.

summary: Maruti Interior Products is Hold — unresolved. The legacy kitchen-hardware franchise is genuine, but the current investment case is not a verified compounder.
